findings.rationale: AZ's local performance at round 20 shows a large calibration-in-the-large gap (CITL -0.34, ECE 0.34) with observed prevalence 0.55 against mean predicted risk 0.21, while its AUC (0.817) is within the normal federation range. This is a prevalence/label shift rather than a feature problem: the model's features imply a much lower outcome rate than the one recorded. Its updates are also anomalous (median norm ratio 4.9, mean cos -0.30), and the norm ratio grows steadily over rounds, which is what a persistent prevalence disagreement produces. Round-1 CITL from drift_by_round (-0.26) suggests the shift is present from the start. Feature shift is small, so this is not drift.

UT's round-20 local metrics show CITL -0.30, ECE 0.27 and observed prevalence 0.45 against a pooled prevalence of 0.149, while AUC (0.835) is normal. The features do not imply this outcome rate, so the label prevalence is shifted. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 3.3, mean cos -0.30), with the norm ratio rising over rounds. The per-round drift CITL estimates are noisy, so onset is set to round 1 with moderate confidence.

WA's round-20 local metrics show CITL -0.31, ECE 0.31 and observed prevalence 0.50 against mean predicted risk 0.20, while AUC (0.821) is normal. This is a prevalence shift that the features do not explain. WA's updates are the most anomalous in the federation (median norm ratio 6.9, mean cos -0.40). The norm ratio climbs from 0.71 in round 1 to 8.4 in round 20, and the cosine turns negative from round 2, consistent with a persistent label-prevalence disagreement with the global model. CITL is already negative in round 1 in the per-round drift data.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspicions with per-client queries. AZ, UT and WA stand out on every screen: CITL about -0.30 to -0.34, observed prevalence 0.45-0.55 against a pooled 0.149, and mean predicted risk far below observed. Their AUCs are normal, so the fault is a prevalence shift, not label noise or poisoning. Their updates are also anomalous (norm ratios 3-7, negative cosine), which follows from training on shifted labels. Subgroup O/E ratios for these three are high across both sexes, consistent with the overall prevalence shift rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Feature-level outliers elsewhere (e.g. GU, AL, AK Sex means, DC BMI, UT Income) are small-client or single-statistic deviations with |z_noise| mostly 3-4.5 and no corroborating performance, update or drift signal, so I did not report them. GU's erratic per-round cosines were too noisy at epsilon 1 to support a free-rider claim. The budget is now fully spent (0.0 left).
